findings.why: This is an explicit skin-lightening claim: it sets lighter skin as the goal, which breaches ASCI's skin-lightening guidelines. Paired with 'Perfect for underarms, neck, and body', it frames naturally darker areas as a problem to be lightened.
findings.fix: Remove the lightening framing entirely, e.g. 'Helps fade the look of dark spots for a more even-looking tone'.

findings.why: The ad never names an active, concentration or mechanism. It could belong to any skincare brand.
findings.fix: Name the hero active and its percentage as printed on the pack, and say what it does.

rule_hit_review.why: 'INSTANTLY' promises an immediate result and needs a study of that duration with its qualifier on the creative. Here it also intensifies a lightening claim (CLM-06).
'fades dark spots in 10 mins' is a specific time-bound result with no study qualifier. 'Fades' is also unhedged; scope it to 'helps fade the look of', with the study shown.
'Instant' here is part of the product name 'Instant Spotlite Mask', not a separate claim. That said, the name reinforces the instant-result promise, and legal may want to review the name itself.
Repeated 🤩 plus ⬇️ make the copy emoji-led, which isn't Minimalist's register.
Three exclamation marks in four short lines is far from the calm, declarative voice.

tone_read: This is high-pressure category copy: 'Don't stress!', all-caps 'INSTANTLY', emoji and a 'Tap to get yours now!' push. It reads nothing like Minimalist's calm, education-first voice.
language_read: No active or concentration is named, the efficacy is unhedged ('fades dark spots'), and the core promise uses lightening vocabulary rather than the brand's 'even-looking tone' language. The headline claim must go before any language polish matters.
